provenance.source: PR #4223 fix: agent memory leak, squash-merged 2025-05-20 as 59940c8b3
provenance.note: The PR stored {count, dispatcher} in the client map so a Client could be evicted once its connections closed, but kOnConnect and kOnDisconnect look the entry up with the origin the event carries, which is client[kUrl] (a URL object), while kDispatch keys the map by String(opts.origin): Map.get misses on every event, count stays 0 and no entry is ever deleted. The later fix #4425 closes over the string key and calls close() instead of destroy(). The base leaked the same way (its own TODO said dispatchers are never removed), so what is new here is bookkeeping that can never fire.

keywords: looked up with a different key
unbounded growth of the client map
the lookup can never find the entry
bugs.note: the connect/disconnect handlers look the entry up with the URL the event carries while the map is keyed by the origin string, so the count never moves and the Client is never evicted

keywords: drops requests that are still queued
should be closed instead of destroyed
destroys a dispatcher that still has work
bugs.note: evicting the Client calls destroy(), which errors the requests still queued on it with ClientDestroyedError; the fix calls close() so the dispatcher drains first. Separate defect from the key mismatch on the two lines above it: with the lookup corrected, one connection-close drops every queued request, so the two are graded as two bugs
